+# Spike: statement export formats
+
+Ticket: BENCH-24. Time box: one day. No production code changes.
+
+## Question
+
+Which file format should a customer get when they export a statement: CSV, OFX or PDF?
+
+## Findings
+
+- CSV is the cheapest. `ledger.statement` already returns every field a row needs: posting time,
+  kind, description, reference, signed amount and running balance. A writer is about 30 lines.
+- OFX needs a stable transaction id per line. `entry_id` is stable, but one entry can have two
+  lines on the same account only for transfers to oneself, which the ledger refuses.
+- PDF needs a layout library that the project does not have. It adds a dependency and a
+  second code path to test, so it is not worth it for a demo bank.
+
+## Recommendation
+
+Build CSV first, behind `GET /api/accounts/{id}/statement.csv`, with amounts as plain decimal
+strings in the account currency. Revisit OFX only when a customer asks for it.
+
+## Out of scope
+
+Scheduled exports, e-mail delivery and a download history.
